docs.title: Welcome to PyToNingans
docs.text:
PyToNingans is an extensible, offline-first desktop idler sandbox game and modding platform built with Python 3.14+ and PySide6 (Qt).

Characters and companions roam, wander, interact, and battle on your Windows desktop, naturally landing and interacting with the top boundaries of non-maximized application windows.

docs.title: Key Features
docs.text:
Desktop SandboxCombat & VisualsCommunity & Modding
  • Transparent Overlay: Frameless, click-through overlay that coexists seamlessly with your daily workflow.
  • Desktop Window Physics: Entities walk, jump, and stand on the borders of your active desktop application windows using low-level Win32 window hit-testing.
  • Dynamic Spawning: Spawn individual entities, full crews, or define desktop spawn exclusion rules.
  • Entity Interactions: Entities can be made to interact with each other, or even your windows as physics, or just detect the window names for dialogue triggers and such.
  • Particle System: Spawn particles for visual flair or make them act as projectiles, with both being able to physically interact with entities and windows on your desktop.
  • Interactive Combat: Characters can battle and unleash animated attacks on your screen.
  • Customizable Feedback: Floating damage popups, proportional health bar impact shaking, numerical HP displays, and auto-hide timing.
  • Minimalistic Themes: I'm not that good of a UI designer, so I made it minimalistic instead.
  • Rich Modpacks: Group multiple entities into cohesive bundles with shared controllers (BaseModPack) and global state.
  • Safety First: Integrated AST security analyzer checks imported packages for prohibited modules before execution.
  • Offline-First Mod Browser: Discover, install, rate, and update community mods without mandatory logins.
  • Upload Your Mods: You can publish your own mods if you login with a verified sign-in provider.
  • Cloud Sync: Optional Supabase Cloud integration with sign-in for Google and Github, and Git-like release versioning.

docs.title: About
docs.text:
An app about putting little creatures on your desktop... Like Teto :)

That was the original premise, but now the "app" has now taken a new form! It resembles a game more, so it's now more of an Idler Sandbox Game.

Initially, this app was supposed to be made with Flutter, but after testing its performance, I have concluded that it would be better to try a different GUI framework, that supports multiple window instances, that focuses more on performance. The Flutter version does work, but the issue with that, is that each new window instance has their own Flutter engine, which means that it's not exactly lightweight.

And that's how this app was born... After searching for some easy to setup GUI frameworks, one of them was the Python version of Qt; PySide6. I have tried this before with C++, but the issue with that, was I'm not that good with C++ yet, and was also my very first language (and GUI framework used), which dates back a couple of years ago...

Now you might ask yourself, what does PyToNingans mean? Well, it's literally just a combination of puns and acronyms:

docs.title: Privacy Policy
docs.text:
Effective Date: October 20, 2026 Project Repository: https://github.com/Meta-Dusk/pytoningans

PyToNingans is an open-source desktop idler sandbox game and modding platform developed by MetaDusk. We respect your privacy and are committed to protecting any personal information you provide when using our services.

docs.title: 1. Information We Collect
docs.text:
PyToNingans is designed as an offline-first application. You do not need to provide any personal data or create an account to use the application or download local mods.

If you choose to sign in using Google OAuth or create a community creator account to publish mods:

  • Account Information: We receive your Google account email address, display name, and avatar image URL via standard Google OAuth 2.0 (openid, email, profile scopes).
  • Creator Profile: We store your creator handle, published mods, and community mod ratings.

We do not collect passwords (when signing in via Google OAuth), payment information, device identifiers, or tracking telemetry.

docs.title: 2. How We Use Your Information
docs.text:
Any information collected is used strictly to:

  • Authenticate your identity as a verified mod author.
  • Associate community mods, modpacks, releases, and reviews with your creator handle.
  • Prevent duplicate accounts and abusive or spam community uploads.

We do not sell, rent, trade, or share your personal information with third-party advertisers or data brokers.

docs.title: 3. Third-Party Services
docs.text:
We utilize the following infrastructure providers to support authentication and community mod hosting:

  • Google OAuth 2.0: Handles user authentication. Google's privacy policy can be viewed at https://policies.google.com/privacy.
  • Supabase: Provides secure cloud database storage and authentication session tokens for published community mods. Supabase's privacy policy can be viewed at https://supabase.com/privacy.

docs.title: 4. Data Retention and Deletion
docs.text: Your profile information is retained for as long as your creator account remains active. You may request deletion of your account and associated published mods at any time by contacting us.

Source code in src/pytoningans/core/api/behaviors.py 
class BaseEntityBehavior:
    """
    Inherit from this class in your entity's `behavior.py`.
    Override any of the hook methods below to implement custom AI logic, interactions,
    combat rules, or dialogue responses.
    """
    def on_spawn(self, entity: IEntity) -> None:
        """Called once when the entity is instantiated and placed in a world."""
        pass

    def on_update(self, entity: IEntity, dt: int) -> None:
        """Called every frame tick. Use for real-time timers and state monitoring."""
        pass

    def on_decision_tick(self, entity: IEntity) -> bool:
        """
        Called when the engine's AI brain evaluates a wander or action decision.
        Return True to override default engine movement/action behavior.
        """
        return False

    def on_interact(self, entity: IEntity, other_entity: IEntity) -> bool:
        """
        Called when this entity collides with or approaches another living entity.
        Return True to override the default social interaction.
        """
        return False

    def on_item_interact(self, entity: IEntity, item: IItem) -> bool:
        """
        Called when this entity collides with or touches an item on the ground.
        Return True to override default collision handling (e.g. automatically picking up).
        """
        return False

    def on_seek_item(self, entity: IEntity, available_items: list[IItem]) -> Optional[IItem] | bool:
        """
        Called when the entity evaluates seeking an item (e.g. survival or scavenging).
        - Return a specific IItem to actively pathfind towards it.
        - Return True to indicate custom seeking was handled (skips default search).
        - Return False or None to allow default survival seeking (e.g. seeking healing items when low on HP) to run.
        """
        return None

    def on_speak(self, entity: IEntity, text: str) -> None:
        """Called whenever this entity speaks dialogue via say() or force_talk()."""
        pass

    def on_damage(self, entity: IEntity, amount: int) -> None:
        """Called when the entity takes damage."""
        pass

    def on_death(self, entity: IEntity) -> None:
        """Called immediately after the entity's health drops to 0."""
        pass

    def on_revive(self, entity: IEntity) -> None:
        """Called when the entity is revived from death."""
        pass

    def on_attack(self, entity: IEntity, target: IEntity) -> bool:
        """
        Called when the entity initiates an attack against target.
        Return True to override engine combat resolution.
        """
        return False

    def on_state_change(self, entity: IEntity, old_state: str, new_state: str) -> None:
        """Called whenever the entity's state changes (e.g. idle -> moving)."""
        pass

    def on_hover_enter(self, entity: IEntity) -> None:
        """Called when the mouse cursor enters the entity's bounding area."""
        pass

    def on_hover_leave(self, entity: IEntity) -> None:
        """Called when the mouse cursor leaves the entity's bounding area."""
        pass

    def on_cursor_grabbed(self, entity: IEntity) -> None:
        """Called when this entity grabs control of the OS mouse cursor."""
        pass

    def on_cursor_released(self, entity: IEntity) -> None:
        """Called when this entity releases the OS mouse cursor."""
        pass

class BaseItemBehavior:
    """
    Inherit from this class in your item's `behavior.py`.
    Override hook methods below to implement custom item effects, pickup validation,
    consumption logic, and entity interaction responses.
    """
    def on_spawn(self, item: IItem) -> None:
        """Called once when the item is instantiated and placed in a world."""
        pass

    def on_update(self, item: IItem, dt: int) -> None:
        """Called every frame tick."""
        pass

    def on_pickup(self, item: IItem, entity: IEntity) -> bool:
        """
        Called when a living entity attempts to pick up this item.
        Return True to allow pickup, False to cancel/reject it.
        """
        return True

    def on_use(self, item: IItem, entity: Optional[IEntity]) -> bool:
        """
        Called when the item is used by its holder or triggered via context menu.
        Return True if the item was successfully used/consumed.
        """
        return True

    def on_drop(self, item: IItem, entity: Optional[IEntity]) -> None:
        """Called when this item is dropped by its holder or released."""
        pass

    def on_interact(self, item: IItem, entity: IEntity) -> bool:
        """
        Called when a living entity collides with or touches this item on the ground.
        Return True to override default collision handling.
        """
        return False

    def on_state_change(self, item: IItem, old_state: str, new_state: str) -> None:
        """Called when the item's operational state changes."""
        pass

    def on_hover_enter(self, item: IItem) -> None:
        """Called when the mouse cursor enters the item's bounding area."""
        pass

    def on_hover_leave(self, item: IItem) -> None:
        """Called when the mouse cursor leaves the item's bounding area."""
        pass

    def on_destroy(self, item: IItem) -> None:
        """Called when the item is removed from the world or destroyed."""
        pass

@runtime_checkable
class IBaseEntity(Protocol):
    """Foundational interface for all entities and structures rendered on desktop."""
    mod_manager: Optional[IModInfo]
    world: Optional[IWorld]
    facing_left: bool
    sprite_rotation: float
    velocity_y: float
    move_speed: float
    fade_in_on_spawn: bool
    can_climb_walls: bool
    can_move_windows: bool
    ignore_window_physics: bool
    should_use_window_physics: bool
    is_climbing: bool
    is_cursor_grabbed: bool
    is_following_cursor: bool
    target_pos: Optional[Any]
    components: dict[str, IComponent]

    @property
    def state(self) -> str:
        """Returns the current state string of the entity."""
        ...

    @state.setter
    def state(self, value: Union[str, EntityState, StructureState, ItemState]) -> None:
        """Transitions the entity to a new state, updating animation and callbacks."""
        ...

    def x(self) -> float:
        """Current X coordinate in world scene space."""
        ...

    def y(self) -> float:
        """Current Y coordinate in world scene space."""
        ...

    def setPos(self, x: float, y: float) -> None:
        """Directly positions the entity in world scene space."""
        ...

    def move(self, x: float, y: float) -> None:
        """Alias for setPos(x, y)."""
        ...

    def width(self) -> int:
        """Current pixel width of the entity's visual bounding box."""
        ...

    def height(self) -> int:
        """Current pixel height of the entity's visual bounding box."""
        ...

    def toFront(self) -> None:
        """Brings the entity forward in the scene visual stacking order."""
        ...

    def destroy(self) -> None:
        """Removes the entity from the world, detaches components, and cleans up memory."""
        ...

    def fade_in(self, duration_ms: int = 1000) -> None:
        """Smoothly fades in the entity from current opacity to 1.0."""
        ...

    def fade_out(self, duration_ms: int = 1000, destroy_on_complete: bool = False) -> None:
        """Smoothly fades out the entity from current opacity to 0.0."""
        ...

    def flip(self) -> None:
        """Toggles horizontal facing direction and horizontally mirrors collision hitboxes."""
        ...

    def sceneBoundingRect(self) -> IRect:
        """Returns the absolute scene bounding box of the entity."""
        ...

    def move_window(self, win: IRect, dx: int, dy: int) -> bool:
        """Moves the specified desktop window by (dx, dy) pixels."""
        ...

    #? Cursor Interaction API
    def get_cursor_pos(self) -> tuple[float, float]:
        """Returns the current OS mouse cursor position mapped into this entity's world scene coordinates."""
        ...

    def get_global_cursor_pos(self) -> tuple[int, int]:
        """Returns the current OS mouse cursor coordinates in virtual desktop space."""
        ...

    def set_cursor_pos(self, scene_x: float, scene_y: float) -> None:
        """Moves the OS mouse cursor to the given position in world scene coordinates."""
        ...

    def grab_cursor(
        self,
        offset_x: Optional[int] = None,
        offset_y: Optional[int] = None,
        duration_ms: Optional[int] = None,
    ) -> None:
        """Grabs the OS mouse cursor, locking it to the entity's position (+ offset) as it moves."""
        ...

    def release_cursor(self) -> None:
        """Releases the OS mouse cursor if currently grabbed by this entity."""
        ...

    def follow_cursor(self, enabled: bool = True, min_distance: float = 30.0) -> None:
        """Configures the entity to automatically follow / pathfind towards the mouse cursor."""
        ...

    #? Component Management
    def add_component(self, component: IComponent) -> IComponent:
        """Attaches and registers a component to this entity."""
        ...

    def get_component(self, name: str) -> Optional[IComponent]:
        """Retrieves an attached component by name, or None if not present."""
        ...

    def has_component(self, name: str) -> bool:
        """Checks if a component with the specified name is attached."""
        ...

    def remove_component(self, name: str) -> Optional[IComponent]:
        """Detaches and returns the component with the given name, or None."""
        ...

    is_force_idle: bool
    is_physics_enabled: bool
    is_hovered: bool
    is_dragged: bool
    is_interactable: bool
    instance_name: Optional[str]
    display_name: str
    identification: str

    def set_force_idle(self, enabled: bool) -> None:
        """Toggles force-idle state where the entity plays idle animations but disables AI and gravity."""
        ...

    def set_instance_name(self, name: Optional[str]) -> None:
        """Sets a unique instance name for this entity."""
        ...

    def update_tooltip(self) -> None:
        """Updates the item tooltip to match its entity identification."""
        ...

    #? Entity Tags
    tags: set[str]

    def has_tag(self, tag: str) -> bool:
        """Returns True if the entity has the specified tag (case-insensitive)."""
        ...

    def has_all_tags(self, *tags: str) -> bool:
        """Returns True if the entity contains every specified tag."""
        ...

    def has_any_tag(self, *tags: str) -> bool:
        """Returns True if the entity contains at least one of the specified tags."""
        ...

    def add_tag(self, tag: str) -> None:
        """Dynamically adds a tag to the entity at runtime."""
        ...

    def remove_tag(self, tag: str) -> None:
        """Removes a tag from the entity at runtime."""
        ...

@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True, kw_only=True)
class ParticleConfigDTO:
    """
    Data Transfer Object (DTO) for the ParticleConfig.\n
    Single source of truth for particle visual, physical, and collision properties."""

    # Physics & Lifetime
    gravity: float = 0.0
    """Applied vertical velocity."""
    lifetime: float = 3.0
    """Duration in seconds."""

    # Visual FX Toggles
    fade_out: bool = True
    """Fade out on expire."""
    scale_over_time: float = 1.0
    """Scale multiplier over time."""
    rotation_speed: float = 0.0
    """Rotation speed in degrees clockwise."""

    # Motion & Steering & Tags
    tags: set[str] = field(default_factory=set)
    initial_rotation_range: tuple[float, float] = (0.0, 0.0)
    orient_to_velocity: bool = False
    """Force look at velocity's direction."""
    homing_target: Optional[IGraphicsItem] = None
    """Optional target to home into."""
    homing_speed: float = 0.0

    # Collision & Hierarchy Toggles
    local_space: bool = False
    """Force local space transformation (inherit parent's location)."""
    bounce_bounds: bool = True
    """Bounce back upon hitting boundaries."""
    passthrough_mouse: bool = True
    """Ignore OS mouse interactions."""
    collide_windows: bool = False
    """Allow collision with OS windows."""
    collide_entities: bool = False
    """Allow collision with entities."""

    # Callbacks & Sub-Emitters
    on_hit_window: OptionalOnHitWindowCallback = None
    """Called upon hitting an OS window."""
    on_hit_entity: OptionalOnHitEntityCallback = None
    """Called upon hitting an entity."""
    on_expire: OptionalOnExpireCallback = None
    """Called upon duration expiration."""
    on_particle_expire_emitter: OptionalOnParticleExpireEmitterCallback = None
    """Called upon particle emitter expiration."""

    @classmethod
    def from_emitter_config(
        cls,
        emitter_cfg: ParticleEmitterConfigDTO,
        *,
        gravity: float,
        lifetime: float,
        scale_target: float,
        rotation_speed: float,
    ) -> ParticleConfigDTO:
        """Constructs a resolved ParticleConfig from a ParticleEmitterConfig template."""
        return cls(
            gravity=gravity,
            lifetime=lifetime,
            fade_out=emitter_cfg.fade_out,
            scale_over_time=scale_target,
            rotation_speed=rotation_speed,
            tags=emitter_cfg.tags or set(),
            initial_rotation_range=emitter_cfg.initial_rotation_range,
            orient_to_velocity=emitter_cfg.orient_to_velocity,
            homing_target=emitter_cfg.homing_target,
            homing_speed=emitter_cfg.homing_speed,
            local_space=emitter_cfg.local_space,
            bounce_bounds=emitter_cfg.bounce_bounds,
            passthrough_mouse=emitter_cfg.passthrough_mouse,
            collide_windows=emitter_cfg.collide_windows,
            collide_entities=emitter_cfg.collide_entities,
            on_hit_window=emitter_cfg.on_hit_window,
            on_hit_entity=emitter_cfg.on_hit_entity,
            on_expire=emitter_cfg.on_expire,
            on_particle_expire_emitter=emitter_cfg.on_particle_expire_emitter,
        )

class ParticlePresets:
    """
    A helper class that wraps the particle manager. Provides access to example implementations.
    """
    def __init__(self, particle_manager: IParticleManager) -> None:
        """The real ParticleManager instance can be found in a IWorld instance."""
        self.manager: IParticleManager = particle_manager

    def explode(
        self,
        texture: ResolvableTexture,
        pos: Pos2D,
        count: int = 30,
        speed: float = 300.0,
        gravity: float = 200.0,
        lifetime: float = 1.2,
        collide_windows: bool = False,
        collide_entities: bool = False,
        on_hit_entity: OptionalOnHitEntityCallback = None,
    ) -> list[IParticle]:
        """Creates a radial burst of particles that arc outward with gravity."""
        config = ParticleEmitterConfigDTO(
            pixmap=texture,
            pos=pos,
            velocity_x_range=(-speed, speed),
            velocity_y_range=(-speed, speed),
            gravity_range=(gravity, gravity * 1.5),
            lifetime_range=(lifetime * 0.5, lifetime),
            scale_over_time_range=(0.2, 0.8),
            fade_out=True,
            collide_windows=collide_windows,
            collide_entities=collide_entities,
            on_hit_entity=on_hit_entity,
        )
        emitter: IParticleEmitter = self.manager.create_emitter(config)
        return emitter.burst(count)

    def dust_trail(
        self,
        texture: ResolvableTexture,
        pos: Pos2D = Pos2D(0, 0),
        target: Optional[IGraphicsItem] = None,
        offset: Pos2D = Pos2D(0, 0),
        rate: float = 15.0,
        duration: Optional[float] = None,
    ) -> IParticleEmitter:
        """Spawns soft, rising dust particles attached to a moving target or position."""
        config = ParticleEmitterConfigDTO(
            pixmap=texture,
            pos=pos,
            target=target,
            offset=offset,
            rate=rate,
            duration=duration,
            velocity_x_range=(-20.0, 20.0),
            velocity_y_range=(-40.0, -10.0),
            gravity_range=(0.0, 0.0),
            lifetime_range=(0.4, 0.8),
            scale_over_time_range=(1.2, 1.8),
            fade_out=True,
            bounce_bounds=False,
            passthrough_mouse=True,
        )
        return self.manager.create_emitter(config)

    def spark_impact(
        self,
        texture: ResolvableTexture,
        pos: Pos2D,
        count: int = 12,
    ) -> list[IParticle]:
        """Fast, short-lived sparks emitted when a projectile hits a window or entity."""
        config = ParticleEmitterConfigDTO(
            pixmap=texture,
            pos=pos,
            velocity_x_range=(-250.0, 250.0),
            velocity_y_range=(-250.0, 250.0),
            gravity_range=(100.0, 300.0),
            lifetime_range=(0.15, 0.35),
            rotation_speed_range=(-360.0, 360.0),
            scale_over_time_range=(0.1, 0.5),
            fade_out=True,
            bounce_bounds=False,
            passthrough_mouse=True,
        )
        emitter: IParticleEmitter = self.manager.create_emitter(config)
        return emitter.burst(count)

    def ambient_aura(
        self,
        texture: ResolvableTexture,
        pos: Pos2D = Pos2D(0, 0),
        target: Optional[IGraphicsItem] = None,
        offset: Pos2D = Pos2D(0, 0),
        radius: float = 25.0,
        rate: float = 10.0,
        local_space: bool = False
    ) -> IParticleEmitter:
        """Orbiting/floating particles."""
        config = ParticleEmitterConfigDTO(
            pixmap=texture,
            pos=pos,
            target=target,
            offset=offset,
            local_space=local_space,
            rate=rate,
            spawn_radius=radius,
            velocity_x_range=(-15.0, 15.0),
            velocity_y_range=(-30.0, -5.0),
            gravity_range=(-20.0, 0.0),
            lifetime_range=(1.5, 3.0),
            scale_over_time_range=(0.5, 1.0),
            fade_out=True,
            bounce_bounds=False,
            passthrough_mouse=True,
        )
        return self.manager.create_emitter(config)

Passing a tuple will need the first member as the shape. You can omit the rest, which will have defaults.

("dot", radius, color); defaults to radius=6, color="white"

("glow_circle" or "glow", size, core_color, outer_color); defaults to

size=15, core_color="white", outer_color="transparent"

An alternative is a oneline string, that is colon-separated. Except, it must start with 'procedural:'.

docs.title: Building & Requirements
docs.text: PyToNingans is developed for Windows environments and requires Python 3.14+ alongside PySide6. This section is intended for people who intends to build the project from source. If you just want to download the installer for the application, please refer to the Releases section in the GitHub repository.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
Before running PyToNingans, ensure you have:

  1. Operating System: Windows 10 or Windows 11 (64-bit).
  2. Python: Python 3.14 or newer.
  3. Package Manager: uv (recommended for instant dependency resolution and execution).

docs.title: Building with uv (Recommended)
docs.text:
1. Clone the Repository:
git clone https://github.com/Meta-Dusk/pytoningans.git
cd pytoningans
  1. Sync Dependencies: uv automatically installs the appropriate PySide6 wheels matching your Python interpreter:
uv sync
  1. Launch the App:
uv run py src/pytoningans/main.py

or

uv run pytoningans

docs.title: Standalone Executable Deployment
docs.text:
PyToNingans includes a complete standalone deployment specification via Nuitka (pysidedeploy.spec).

To compile an optimized, standalone Windows .exe:

pyside6-deploy -c pysidedeploy.spec

The output executable will be placed in the build/ directory with all assets and required Qt plugins bundled.

docs.title: Documentation Local Preview
docs.text:
To build and preview this documentation website locally on your machine:

uv run --group docs mkdocs serve

Open your browser at http://127.0.0.1:8000/ to browse with instant live reloading.

docs.title: Installation & Requirements
docs.text: PyToNingans is initially built for Windows environments, which means that I haven't tested the app in other Operating Systems. Setting up the app is very straightforward, as you only need to download the installer in the Releases section in the GitHub repository!

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
Before installing PyToNingans, ensure you have:

  • Operating System: Windows 10 or Windows 11 (64-bit).

That's mostly it for now.

docs.title: Setup Instructions
docs.text:
You would usually see the setup instructions in the note included in the release, but by default, what you would expect is basically an executable named; PyToNingans-vX.X.X-Win64-Installer.exe. The Xs simply represents the version numbers. You will also expect another executable, which is similary named; PyToNingans-vX.X.X-with-console-Win64-Installer.exe. This version simply just has a console built-in (which is just for debugging). You don't really need this version, unless you need to see the logs of the app.

Once you download the installer, you can just simply follow the setup wizard, and that's it! It's that easy :)

docs.title: Updates
docs.text: For now, there's no automatic downloading of updates, but updating the app isn't that difficult. You can just simply reinstall the app with the latest version of the installer, and it will handle updating it! This is all thanks to Inno Setup Compiler :)

docs.title: Quickstart Guide
docs.text: Get up and running with PyToNingans in minutes!

docs.title: The Control Panel
docs.text:
When PyToNingans launches, the central Control Panel appears. It provides intuitive modular controls divided into two main panels:

+-------------------------------------------------------+
| Control Panel                                     [X] |
+---------------------------+---------------------------+
| Spawning & Placement      | Live Stats & Controls     |
| - Entity Selector         | - Active Entities: 3      |
| - Spawn Area Filter       | - FPS / System Performance|
| - [Spawn Selected] Button | - Kill All / Pause All    |
|                           +---------------------------+
|                           | Management & Settings     |
|                           | - [Mod Browser]           |
|                           | - [Manage Mods]           |
|                           | - [Settings]              |
|                           | - [Theme]  [Shutdown]     |
+---------------------------+---------------------------+

docs.title: 1. Spawning Your First Entity
docs.text:
1. Look at the left pane (Spawning and Placement).
  2. Select any installed mod entity or pre-packaged companion from the list.
  3. Choose your desired spawn boundary:
    • Full Primary Screen: Spawns anywhere across your monitor.
    • Active Desktop Bounds: Prefers empty space away from foreground taskbars.
  4. Click Spawn Entity. Your character will drop directly onto your desktop!

docs.title: 2. Interacting With Characters
docs.text:
• Left Click & Drag: Pick up any entity and throw or reposition them anywhere across your monitors.
  • Right Click: Opens the Entity Context Menu to inspect current stats, view assigned animations, trigger special actions, or despawn the character.
  • Desktop Windows: Drag a desktop window (like Notepad or a browser) underneath a falling character; watch them land and walk across the top title bar of your application!

docs.title: 3. Managing Mods and Settings
docs.text:
• Mod Browser: Click Mod Browser to discover, download, and rate community creations.
  • Manage Mods: Open the local Mod Manager Hub to toggle, edit, or create new sprite sheets.
  • Settings: Open the Settings menu to customize health bars, damage popups, window physics, and enable Developer Mode.

docs.title: Modpacks & Shared Controllers
docs.text: In addition to single-character mods, PyToNingans supports Modpacks—multi-entity bundles capable of executing coordinated behaviors, shared team mechanics, and synchronized events.

docs.title: Modpack Directory Layout
docs.text:
A Modpack bundles multiple entities under a shared controller:

mods/
└── vocaloid_crew_pack/
    ├── pack.json            # Modpack manifest and entity roster
    ├── pack.py              # Shared controller inheriting BaseModPack
    └── entities/            # Contained entity subdirectories
        ├── hatsune_miku/
        │   ├── config.json
        │   └── sprite_sheet.png
        ├── kagamine_rin/
        │   ├── config.json
        │   └── sprite_sheet.png
        └── kagamine_len/
            ├── config.json
            └── sprite_sheet.png

  "id": "vocaloid_crew_pack",

docs.title: The Shared Controller (pack.py)
docs.text:
Every Modpack can define a pack.py script that extends BaseModPack:

"""Shared controller for Vocaloid Desktop Companions."""
from api import BaseModPack, PackMenuAction

class PackController(BaseModPack):
    """Coordinates behavior and shared abilities across all pack members."""

    def on_pack_loaded(self) -> None:
        print(f"Modpack {self.name} loaded with {len(self.entities)} entities!")

    def on_entity_spawned(self, entity_id: str) -> None:
        # Example: Play a fanfare when a pack member joins the desktop
        pass

    def get_custom_actions(self) -> list[PackMenuAction]:
        """Provides custom context menu actions shared across pack members."""
        return [
            PackMenuAction(
                label="Sing Duet",
                callback=self._trigger_duet_routine,
                tooltip="Synchronize dancing and singing animations"
            )
        ]

    def _trigger_duet_routine(self) -> None:
        # Custom coordination logic
        pass

docs.title: Key Controller Lifecycle Hooks
docs.text:
• on_pack_loaded(): Called when the pack is registered into the game session.
  • on_entity_spawned(entity_id): Fired whenever a member of the pack is spawned.
  • on_pack_unloaded(): Cleanup hook when the pack is uninstalled or deactivated.
  • get_custom_actions(): Returns action buttons added to the context menu of all member characters.

docs.title: Security Audit & AST Sandbox
docs.text: Because community mods and modpacks can include Python scripts (pack.py), security and sandboxing are critical. PyToNingans provides an automated AST (Abstract Syntax Tree) Security Analyzer and visual Mod Inspector.

docs.title: The Mod Inspector
docs.text:
Before installing or running any mod, you can inspect it directly inside the Mod Browser by clicking the Inspect button:

  • File Hierarchy: Browse package assets, sprites, audio files, and scripts before extracting.
  • Manifest Viewer: Review configuration parameters, required engine versions, and authors.
  • Source Code Viewer: Inspect Python script contents with syntax highlighting.
  • AST Security Audit: Review automated safety verdicts and audit reports.

docs.title: AST Security Rules
docs.text: The AST Security Analyzer statically parses Python code without executing it. It checks for unsafe operations and assigns one of three safety ratings:

docs.title: Clean / Passed
docs.text: No suspicious imports or restricted system calls detected. Safe for execution.

docs.title: Warning
docs.text: Uses dynamic attribute access (getattr, eval) or unusual reflection. Permitted, but highlighted for user review.

docs.title: Prohibited / Blocked
docs.text:
Attempts to import or invoke dangerous system modules:

  • subprocess, os.system, shutil.rmtree
  • Network sockets (socket, raw HTTP callers outside approved clients)
  • Direct low-level process memory modification
flowchart TD
    Mod[Community Mod Package] --> Parser[AST Static Analysis]
    Parser --> CheckImports{Dangerous Imports?}
    CheckImports -->|Yes: subprocess, socket, etc.| Block[Flagged as Dangerous / Blocked]
    CheckImports -->|No| CheckCalls{Suspicious Reflection?}
    CheckCalls -->|Yes: eval, exec| Warn[Audit Warning]
    CheckCalls -->|No| Pass[Audit Passed]

The config_version field tracks schema compatibility. The current version is defined by CURRENT_CONFIG_VERSION (10).

If a community mod was authored for an older schema version, the Community Mod Browser flags it with an Outdated Config (vX) warning tag, helping users make informed download decisions.

docs.title: Community Hub & Cloud Publishing
docs.text: The Community Mod Browser connects players with creators. You can discover, install, update, rate, and publish community creations seamlessly.

docs.title: Offline-First Architecture
docs.text:
PyToNingans operates offline-first:

  • You do not need an account or internet connection to use the app, manage local mods, or test custom companions.
  • The browser launches instantly into Offline Catalog mode using local disk cache.
  • Click Connect to Cloud at any time to sync live releases from the community Supabase database.
  • Click Work Offline to immediately revert to local cache.

docs.title: Creator Accounts & Authentication
docs.text:
To publish mods or submit ratings, creators authenticate to prevent impersonation and spam uploads:

  1. Email & Password: Standard account registration with client confirmation.
  2. Continue with Google: Secure OAuth 2.0 login in your default browser.
  3. Continue in Offline Mode: For offline testing, set up a local creator profile (@LocalCreator) without cloud credentials.

docs.title: Git-Like Release Management
docs.text:
When publishing a mod or modpack, PyToNingans manages versions like a version control system:

flowchart LR
    v1["Release v1.0.0
(Initial Launch)"] --> v2["Release v1.1.0
(New Animations)"]
    v2 --> v3["Release v1.2.0
(Dual Duet Routine)"]
  • No Duplicate Uploads: Publishing a mod with an existing ID automatically appends a new entry to that mod's mod_releases table.
  • Changelogs: Each release tracks its own version notes and target compatibility (target_app_version, config_version).
  • One-Click Update: Users with an installed older version see an Update button on the mod card, automatically downloading and replacing older files.
  • Rating System: Community scores range from 1.0 to 10.0, averaged in real time.

docs.title: Combat & Visual Feedback
docs.text: PyToNingans features a dynamic combat feedback system designed to provide responsive visual indicators while keeping screen clutter minimal.

docs.title: Health Bar Display Modes
docs.text:
You can tailor how and when character health bars are rendered on screen:

Mode Behavior Best Used For Show On Damage Only (Default) Health bars remain invisible until a character takes damage, staying visible for a configurable duration before fading out. Distraction-free daily work and clean desktops. Always Visible Health bars are pinned above characters permanently. Active battles, boss fights, or testing stats. Hidden / Disabled Completely disables health bar rendering. Minimalist aesthetic.

docs.title: Floating Damage Numbers
docs.text: When an attack connects, animated floating numbers pop up and float upward above the target, displaying the exact damage dealt with critical hit emphasis.

docs.title: Damage Impact Shake
docs.text: Taking a heavy hit causes the health bar to shake proportionally to the damage taken relative to maximum health.

docs.title: Numerical HP Display
docs.text: Toggles the numerical display of current health and maximum health (e.g., 85 / 100) centered directly inside the health bar gauge.

docs.title: Configuring Feedback
docs.text: All visual combat features are customizable in Settings $\rightarrow$ Combat & Visuals. Adjustments apply instantly to all active entities without restarting the game.

docs.title: Desktop Window Physics
docs.text: One of the standout features of PyToNingans is its real-time desktop environment collision system. Characters do not merely walk across the bottom of your monitor—they recognize other running desktop applications as physical obstacles and platforms.

docs.title: How Window Collision Works
docs.text:
PyToNingans interfaces directly with the native Windows desktop manager via the Win32 API (user32.dll):

  1. Window Enumeration: The engine queries visible top-level windows on the screen (e.g., text editors, web browsers, file explorers).
  2. Hit-Testing: The engine retrieves window rectangles (GetWindowRect) while filtering out minimized windows, transparent overlays, and fullscreen desktop workers.
  3. Platform Recognition: When an entity falls onto the top edge of a window frame, the physics solver converts the window boundary into a temporary solid platform.
flowchart TD
    Entity[Falling Entity] --> Test{Hit-Testing Desktop Window?}
    Test -->|Above Window Top Border| Land[Land on Window Frame]
    Land --> Walk[Walk across Window Title Bar]
    Test -->|Window Moved or Closed| Fall[Gravity Takes Over & Entity Falls]
    Fall --> Ground[Land on Desktop Taskbar / Monitor Bottom]

docs.title: Configuring Window Physics
docs.text:
You can configure physics behavior dynamically in the Settings dialog under the Combat & Visuals tab:

  • Enable Desktop Window Physics: Check to allow characters to stand and walk on non-maximized application windows.
  • Avoid Spawning Over Open Windows (Spawning Tab): Prevents characters from appearing directly over your active work windows, prioritizing unobstructed desktop regions.

docs.title: Settings & Developer Tools
docs.text: The Application Settings dialog provides a centralized, categorized control hub for personalizing your desktop experience, configuring boundaries, and accessing developer tools.

docs.title: Dialog Layout & Navigation
docs.text:
The settings window is divided into three intuitive tabs:

+-------------------------------------------------------+
| Application Settings                              [X] |
+-------------------------------------------------------+
| [ Combat & Visuals ] [ Spawning ] [ Developer ]       |
+-------------------------------------------------------+
|  ... (scrollable tab content) ...                     |
|                                                       |
|                                                       |
+-------------------------------------------------------+
| [Reset Defaults]                              [Close] |
+-------------------------------------------------------+
  • Auto-Resizing & Scroll Protection: The dialog dynamically auto-sizes based on content and DPI scaling. If your monitor or scaling prevents displaying everything at once, each tab smoothly scrolls without clipping controls or action buttons.
  • Manual Resize Grip: Drag the handle in the bottom-right corner to resize the dialog to your liking.

docs.title: 1. Combat & Visuals Tab
docs.text:
• Health Bar Display Mode: Select between Show On Damage Only, Always Visible, or Hidden.
  • Auto-Hide Delay: Set the timeout (1 to 15 seconds) before health bars fade after taking damage.
  • Floating Damage Numbers: Toggle popup damage counters on hit.
  • Damage Impact Shake: Toggle health bar shaking on impacts.
  • Show HP Values: Toggle numeric HP / Max HP text within the bar.
  • Desktop Window Physics: Toggle solid collision on desktop window title bars.

docs.title: 2. Spawning Tab
docs.text:
• Avoid Spawning Over Open Windows: Directs spawning algorithms to prioritize empty areas of the screen.
  • Spawn Boundary Area: Choose between full screen geometry or active desktop workspace bounds.

docs.title: 3. Developer Mode Tab
docs.text:
Checking Enable Developer Mode unlocks diagnostic testing capabilities:

  • Mod Browser Debug Menu: Adds a Debug ▾ button to the Community Mod Browser top bar.
  • Load Demo / Seed Catalog: Injects the 6 sample demo mods into your local catalog cache for offline testing.
  • Clear Catalog Cache: Wipes local catalog items to test empty state handling.
  • Quick Folder Access: One-click shortcuts to open the App Data directory or local mods/ directory in Windows Explorer.
